title: An RGBA accepted candidate whose scanlines use filters 1–4
why: Its greyscale sibling pins that the filter byte is *read*; this pins that the predictor steps by the pixel stride. With one channel the two are indistinguishable — `bpp` is 1 either way — so an engine with the distance hardcoded decodes that fixture correctly and mis-decodes every ordinary filtered RGB or RGBA candidate in the field. Same pixels as the unfiltered RGBA case, so only the filtering can make the verdict differ.
